questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Language, location, academic opportunities

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the information available to study abroad students is very extensive, and if it doesn't say a specific thing in the flyers, you just have to ask

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The Global Mobility Office was very accomodating and they signed my Proof of Attendance

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Dorms

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Shared kitchen, and special options for vegan students

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's outdated and noisy, but it is often central and the rent is manageable

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I was registered before I arrived in London. And when I arrived I just had to pick up a lanyard to gain access to campus while waiting for my student ID to be shipped

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There are staffed reception at every entrance to every building, so they helped me get around and let me through the gates before my ID arrived

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful, I got all my 1st choices

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start the process from home and fill out the module registration early! it's first come first served, so it benefits to be early

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found that the level of my coursed varied a lot, even though they were all level 6. The lectures and seminars were short and often very superficial in covering the material sufficiently. However, I liked how the seminars were small groups of 6-12 students, making it easier to ask question and do more targeted teachings

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Like i mentioned, the lectures and seminars were only 1 hour, and very superficial. However, the number of students in seminars were much lower than back home, which I really benefited from.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
6SSPP356 - Authoritarianism 
6AAOB509 - Comparative Capitalism
6SSPP341 - Global Power Europe
6SSPP248 - Comparative Political Theory

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: 6SSPP341 - Global Power Europe was a really good course but mostly due to the Professor (Thomas Maltby) who made the lectures and seminars very interesting and insightful.

questions.answer: Travel insurance

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The food and drinks were more expensive than I imagined.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't really attend any societies.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Sports (Gym at Student residences), Dance classes, different buisness-related societies, cultural societies, events

King's also has its own bar at both Guy's and Strand campus, which sell cheap beer and food.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't attend any but heard good things about the Dance Society and the Stand-Up comedy society

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend walking around everywhere to get a sense of where one thing is compared to another! And especially visiting the Parks and residential areas - they are beautiful!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy! However, most students are international, so that made a huge difference

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the mixers at the beginning of the semester. And talk to people in your seminars! Most of the courses that I took were elective, so no one really knew each other, which made it easier to mingle

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really - maybe that they go out every day of the week and not just on the weekends ;)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How easy going it was. And how I didn't feel lost, because it resembled the danish culture a lot - maybe to much!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It's gonna be expensive, it's gonna be lonely at times, but you would want to miss it!

Oh, and the library is lovely!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: King's is very international, so don't expect the full English experience. Furthermore, the teachings vary a lot and I found myself disagreeing with some of the feedback I got, and that is why the ability to go to an office hour with a professor is something you really should take advantage of!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting feedback on all my assignments as well as doing a lot of work alone. and meeting all the other King's and exchange students.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not feeling lonely, and being okay with having long days at the library alone. This was also such a rewarding experience! I really got to work on myself.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
